newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ahmsa '97 sales seen up, exports down.
newsitem.headline: Ahmsa '97 sales seen up, exports down.

text.p: Conglomerate Grupo Acerero del Norte (GAN) forecast lower exports but increased sales by its steelmaking subsidiary Altos Hornos de Mexico (Ahmsa) in 1997, the company vice-president told journalists on Thursday.
Enrique Gasca Neri forecast that total steel sales by Ahmsa in 1997 would increase from "2.8 million to almost 2.9 million tonnes, mainly due to productivity (gains)."
Gasca, who spoke at a steelmakers' congress in Guadalajara, meanwhile expected exports of flat products to fall due to an increase in domestic demand.
"In 1994, we were exporting around 100,000 tonnes and went up to one million tonnes (in 1995)," Gasca said.
"We will close this year with around 800,000 tonnes, and should export around 600,000 tonnes next year," he added.

Gasca said that in nationwide terms Mexico's production will grow to almost 13 million tonnes this year from 11.5 million tonnes of liquid steel in 1992. "We forecast figures rising to 13.6 million tonnes in 1997," he said.
Gasca also expected exports for the sector as a whole in Mexico to fall to 4.7 million tonnes in 1997, down from 5.6 million this year, again due to a recovery in domestic demand.
